what_its_for: This medication is used to treat moderate to severe hot flashes (sudden feelings of warmth, flushing, and sweating) in women going through menopause, especially when estrogen alone has not worked well enough. It combines a female hormone (estrogen) with a small amount of a male hormone (testosterone) to help relieve these symptoms.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablet unless your doctor says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the lowest dose that works for you for the shortest time needed. The usual starting dose is one tablet taken once a day, but your doctor may adjust this based on how you respond and how you feel. There are two strengths available — a regular strength and a half-strength (H.S.) version. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day or close to your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medication at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to safely dispose of them.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking while taking this medicine — smoking greatly increases your risk of serious side effects like blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not start any new prescription, over-the-counter medicines, or herbal supplements (especially St. John's Wort) without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, as they may interact with this medication. Avoid long periods of staying still (such as long flights or bed rest), as this can raise your risk of blood clots.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following warning signs: chest pain or pressure, sudden shortness of breath, severe headache, sudden vision changes or loss, weakness or numbness on one side of your body, sudden slurred speech, pain or swelling in your leg, unusual vaginal bleeding, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), severe stomach pain, a lump in your breast, mood changes or signs of depression, unusual hair growth on the face or body, voice deepening, or acne that is getting worse. Also call your doctor if you develop any new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Most women begin to notice some improvement in their hot flashes within a few weeks of starting this medication. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not feel immediate results. Your doctor will regularly review whether you still need this medicine and at what dose.
special_populations: Older women (over 65): Use with caution, as the risks of serious side effects such as blood clots, stroke, and dementia may be higher in older women. Women with liver problems: This medicine is processed by your liver. Tell your doctor if you have or have had liver disease, as you may need special monitoring or a different treatment. Women with a history of certain cancers: Do not use this medicine if you have or have had breast cancer, uterine (endometrial) cancer, or other hormone-sensitive cancers, unless specifically directed by your doctor. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm the baby. This medicine is not for use in children.
